submitter: bugfix-220 lane (unbuilt_internal_link dispatch rebuilds the container and reads green) — round 1, submitted alongside the commit per the 2026-07-29 ruling
rationale: bugs_open/220, filed by the 206 lane 2026-08-08 and live-REPRODUCED the same day: the phantom-links check deliberately files an unbuilt_internal_link work item against the TARGET page via the item's page_id COLUMN (the never-deployed page the link 404s at), but build-dispatch-loop's call_handler maps page_name from current_item.spec.page_name — the page CONTAINING the link — and never reads page_id. The handler rebuilds/redeploys the container, returns success, mark_complete stamps it, 'complete' is terminal for the dedup index, and the next discovery pass re-mints the same item: a convergence-free green loop that costs a full wrong-page build per cycle (two more live-confirmed 2026-08-08 15:19Z, items 3f066b90/4ba1d4dd). THE CORRECTION THIS PLAN MAKES TO THE BUG FILE'S OWN CANDIDATE 1: 'map page_id? and have load_page_record prefer it' is insufficient as written — load_page_record_action.go resolves page_name FIRST (documented priority, :7-10), and its empty-name branch re-fills the name from input_data.spec.page_name plus three more fallback paths, so for this item type the container's name always resolves and always wins. The forwarded id must carry explicit authority. Per the owner ruling 2026-08-02 (RFC_010 §2: new authority on a shared seam ships as an OPT-IN FIELD with the unsafe default OFF), that authority is a new optional input authoritative_page_id on load_page_record, set by exactly one step config (page-build-handler's, mig 340) — NOT a global priority flip, which would silently change tool-recreation-handler (the only other live agent with this step) and every future config supplying both keys. BLAST RADIUS, measured not argued: (a) the 116 lane's census over all live work items (bug file CONTRIB section) — unbuilt_internal_link is the ONLY item type whose page_id column names a different page from spec.page_name; positive control 13/13 all-history rows disagree, so the live zero is not the empty-set kind. (b) Zero live agents map current_item.page_id in this loop today; input_data.page_id is read only by page-retraction and deduplicate-sections, both with zero work items in all history and neither dispatched by this loop. (c) The mapping shape has an in-fleet PRECEDENT: site-work-orchestrator's call_handler already maps "page_id?": "current_fix_item.page_id" — build-dispatch-loop was the outlier. THE VERIFICATION HALF: VerifyUnbuiltInternalLinkResolved registers for the type under WII-011's fail-closed default. Two disjuncts, per VerifyDeadFragmentLinkResolved's precedent and for the same reason (the item's spec.fix names two remedies): resolved when the container no longer renders the href OR the target has shipped — judged by datahelpers.NeverDeployedPagePredicate, the SAME predicate the detector minted the finding by. Registering it triggers the claim-timeout lockstep obligation (TestRegisteredVerifiersMatchClaimTimeoutExclusion): declared list in sql_for_agents/220 edited in the same commit; live column via mig 341 using 331's targeted-replace template (live list read before writing: the 8-entry form, no drift). ORDERING: both config halves are inert against the pre-roll binary — no live handler dispatched by this loop reads input_data.page_id, and the old binary's LoadPageRecordInputSpec does not declare authoritative_page_id (ExtractActionInputs iterates declared fields; UnknownConfigKeys is an offline audit, not a runtime rejection). Migrations applied immediately; the whole fix arms on the roll. DEFERRED ON RECORD (bug file + register WII-012): candidate 4 — routing an unbuilt target by its page_type through availableBuilders. Package direction blocks cheap reuse (actions imports discovery_checks, so the check cannot import the map back), and with the verifier live a directory-typed target now fails LOUDLY into the attempt machinery (three page-build attempts, then 'failed', two-strike parks re-detections) instead of lying green; the 206 lane's needs_directory path is the designed remediation for those targets. That failed population is the demand signal for whoever takes candidate 4. Tests: green against a clean git archive HEAD overlay (the shared tree carries another session's WIP in the same package). The load-bearing test asserts at the QUERY ARGUMENTS that a resolving container page_name loses to the forwarded target id; a second test pins that WITHOUT the opt-in key, name-first behaviour is byte-for-byte unchanged. Registered as WII-012 in the same commit; LANDMINES entry added for the name-first trap; migration ROLLBACK sidecars for both files.

edits.rationale: The routing authority: new optional input authoritative_page_id. When it resolves and parses as a uuid the lookup is BY ID and the name inputs are ignored; malformed value errors loudly (a misconfigured path — falling through to the name would silently load a different page, the exact defect this closes); absent keeps prior behaviour byte-for-byte. The query/scan/result body is extracted to queryPageRecordRow shared by both paths, so the id path cannot drift from the name path.

The load-bearing test asserts at the QUERY ARGUMENTS — where the wrong page is chosen — that a resolving container page_name loses to the forwarded target id. A second test pins name-first behaviour unchanged without the opt-in key (what licenses shipping the field without an RFC); a third pins the loud error on a malformed value.

edits.rationale: The completion verifier, next to the arm that mints the type. Fail-closed (WII-011 zero policy). Resolved when the container no longer renders the href (the item's own alternative remedy — refusing it would strand a fixed item) OR when the target has shipped, judged by NeverDeployedPagePredicate, the detector's own predicate. Target row deleted while the link still renders → Resolved:false, NOT an error: a settled judgement (the phantom arm re-classifies next pass), and under fail-closed an error would burn attempts on an unanswerable retry.

Six cases; the load-bearing one is the REFUSAL while the target is still unbuilt — the exact live shape of items 8abc9f8d/3f066b90 (container deployed, target still NULL, item complete at attempt_count 0). Also pins: link-removed passes; target-shipped passes; target-row-gone refuses WITHOUT an error (RFC_017 makes an error block-and-retry, wrong for a settled judgement); site_component surface consults chrome; nil PageID errors (fail-closed).
